wo4-when-it-looks-stale.reason: The steps (wait out the roughly ten-minute cache, reopen the tab, then file Feedback with page name and expected video) are implied in technical prose, never laid out as the three steps the title promises.
wo4-when-it-looks-stale.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. The page is behind, so now what? Three steps. First, give it about ten minutes after the upload, because the app checks the channel about that often. Second, refresh or reopen the tab, since an app left open a long time can still show an old view. Third, if it is still behind, report it through Feedback with the page name and the video you expected.
wo4-when-it-looks-stale.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. The page is behind, so now what? Wait about ten minutes from the upload. Reopen the tab so the view loads fresh. If it is still behind after that, it is a real problem, so file it through Feedback with the page name and the expected video, and your words become the record in the fix queue. The app is built to tell you honest timing rather than pretend to be instant, so a short wait is normal and a long one is worth reporting.

senior.open: The title asks what to do when a page looks behind. Allow about ten minutes after an upload, reopen the tab so it loads fresh, and only then report it.
senior.close: So a short delay is normal and honest. Beyond that window, after a reopen, it is a genuine defect, and a Feedback note with the page name and expected video puts it in the queue to be fixed.

That is what it means for the church to set its own roadmap: the house's own voice, not a vendor's, decides what gets built.

wo3-retire-the-old-site.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Is your church website always a message behind? The old site is, because its video player is pinned to one video, so someone has to swap it by hand every time. One edit stops that: replace it with the channel's uploads playlist, which always plays the newest message first with no upkeep. Then the monthly scramble is over.
wo3-retire-the-old-site.example: ONE ID, TWO LETTERS. The uploads playlist uses the channel id with its first two letters changed. Say a channel id were UCabc123; its uploads list would be UUabc123. Put that into the playlist embed, and the page shows the newest upload first from then on. The month buttons can simply be removed, because The Word tab in the app already sorts every message by month automatically.
wo3-retire-the-old-site.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Is your church website always a message behind? Only while it points at one fixed video. Make the one last edit to the uploads playlist embed, remove the month buttons, and the old page stays current with no monthly work. Its remaining job is to point people to the app, which is now the church's main home on the web: installable, searchable, and live.
